title: Supersession Record
description: §5. 'Superseding, amending, or revoking a stored payment mandate with version lineage and freshness proof' (§9 vocabulary). §4.1: 'A MandatePatch is ephemeral by construction. Durable change is exclusively Section 5 supersession.' The record carries §5.1's four residuals: supersedes = H(previous) lineage with semantic re-baselining; deterministic resolution of the three races; a network-agnostic family head with a stated trust model; and the patch interaction, 'with the deployment required to disclose its nullifier-to-epoch update ordering and the resulting atomicity window, if any.'

allOf.$comment: §5.1: 'amendment carries semantic re-baselining — a new committed E₀ — and not merely parameter change.' A supersede action MUST carry a successor and a re-baseline; a revoke action carries neither.

§5.2: 'for revocation, a synchronous-head-check mode with Δ approaching zero is specified, because the realistic adversary is an agent that reads the principal's communications and can front-run an announced revocation within any tolerance window.'

record_id.description: Identifier of this record within the family's lineage.

action.description: §5. Amendment (with re-baselining) or revocation. §5.1 contrasts ERC-8226, 'which, notably, requires explicit revocation and re-issuance for any scope change, never resets cumulative usage on extension, and, because its enforcement is atomic on-chain, gives no treatment of in-flight resolution.'

supersedes.description: §5.1, 'supersedes = H(previous) lineage over signed natural-language mandates'. Hash of the predecessor mandate version.

successor_mandate_hash.description: §5.1. Hash of the new mandate version for a supersede; explicit null for a revoke.

successor_version.description: §5.1. New version number for a supersede; explicit null for a revoke.

epoch.description: §5.2, §7. The epoch this record advances the family to; 'the epoch head enter[s] the statement as a public input' (§7). Monotonic within the family.

family_head.description: §5.1, third residual: 'a network-agnostic family head, a single hash any rail can check, with the trust model stated rather than assumed.'

head_source.description: §5.2: 'The transparency-log deployment requires cosigned heads or a witness network against split-view equivocation; the issuer-registry deployment states its single-operator trust plainly.' §5.1: 'with the trust model stated rather than assumed.'

cosigned_heads.description: §5.2. MUST be true for a transparency-log deployment.

witnesses.description: §5.2, 'a witness network against split-view equivocation'. Empty array for an issuer registry.

operator_id.description: §5.2. The registry operator for an issuer-registry deployment; explicit null otherwise.

trust_model.description: §5.1, 'with the trust model stated rather than assumed'. E.g. 'single-operator' for an issuer registry, 'cosigned-log-with-witnesses' for a transparency log.

staleness_bound_seconds.description: §5.2: 'a mandate-specified staleness bound Δ ... Δ is a service-level bound, not a euphemism: for amendments, activity within Δ against the prior version is tolerated by design; for revocation, a synchronous-head-check mode with Δ approaching zero is specified.' PROFILE-DEFINED: the value of Δ.

scoring_stack_measurement.description: §3.1. Measurement of the stack under which the new E₀ was computed.

instruction_source_bytes_hash.description: §3.1, 'the immutable source bytes of the instruction' for the amended mandate.

re_baseline.description: §5.1, first residual: 'amendment carries semantic re-baselining — a new committed E₀ — and not merely parameter change.' Explicit null for a revoke.

in_flight_resolution.description: §5.1, second residual: 'deterministic resolution of the three races — authorized before, in flight at, and initiated after supersession — evaluated both at authorization and again at capture or commit time, on asynchronous rails where no atomic check exists.' §5.2: 'Cross-rail immediate finality is not claimed: the consume authority is the linearization point and rails inherit its consistency.' PROFILE-DEFINED: the resolution chosen for each race — the paper requires that it be deterministic and disclosed, not that it take a particular value.

authorized_before.description: §5.1, race one: authorizations completed before the supersession's linearization instant.

in_flight_at.description: §5.1, race two: authorizations in flight at the supersession. §5.2: 'for amendments, activity within Δ against the prior version is tolerated by design.'

initiated_after.description: §5.1, race three: authorizations initiated after the supersession. For a revoke, the successor is the empty set and every such authorization declines.

evaluation_points.description: §5.1, 'evaluated both at authorization and again at capture or commit time'.

voided_patch_nullifiers.description: §7 (v2.3 erratum): "Nullifier derivation is domain-separated over issuer, mandate family, version, patch sequence, checkout, and purpose." The nullifier is deliberately rail-independent: the consume authority of §5.3 keys exactly-once consumption on this value, and a rail-scoped derivation would yield distinct nullifiers for the same patch presented on different rails, defeating the cross-rail guarantee. Rail remains, correctly, in the §6 response-transcript domain separator, where it prevents cross-rail transplantation of signed step-up responses. The text published as Technical Disclosure Commons no. 11517 (v2.2) includes "rail" in this list; that is the erratum.

nullifier_epoch_update_ordering.description: §5.1: 'with the deployment required to disclose its nullifier-to-epoch update ordering'. §8: 'The atomicity window between patch nullification and epoch advancement, if any, and its update ordering are disclosed.' PROFILE-DEFINED: which ordering a deployment uses — the paper requires disclosure, not a particular choice.

atomicity_window_ms.description: §5.1, 'and the resulting atomicity window, if any'. Zero for the 'atomic' ordering.

consume_authority.description: §5.3: 'The mandate family's home registry — wallet or issuer — is the sole linearizable consume authority for patch nullifiers and epoch heads. Cross-rail verifiers check it.'

effective_at.description: §5.2. The linearization instant at the consume authority.

forced_by_patch_exhaustion.description: §4.4: 'After a low, profile-defined mandatory number of patches, supersession is forced.' Optional; present and true when this supersession was forced.

full_context_redisplay.description: §4.4: 'because patch-exhaustion supersession arrives precisely when a fatigued user is most exploitable, it requires full-context re-display of the original mandate together with all accumulated deltas'. Optional; MUST be true when `forced_by_patch_exhaustion` is true.

cooling_off_observed_seconds.description: §4.4: 'a profile-defined cooling-off interval before a durable expansion can be signed.' Optional; the interval actually observed. PROFILE-DEFINED.

render_state_hash.description: §6.3, optional presentation-state attestation over the re-display interface.

attestation_tier.description: §6.3, optional; 'with the software tier declared evidentially weak'.

human_signature.description: §4.1: 'Durable change is exclusively Section 5 supersession' — and it is the principal who signs it. §6.2 domain separation applies.

anchor.description: Independent evidence that a signature existed at its `signed_at`. OPTIONAL but RECOMMENDED: routine verification can rely on a self-asserted `signed_at`, but dispute-grade evidence cannot, because a self-asserted timestamp is asserted by the one party with an incentive to misstate it. PROFILE-DEFINED: profile v1 anchors into the §5.2 transparency log rather than standing up a second log — §5.2 already requires 'cosigned heads or a witness network against split-view equivocation', which is precisely the property a time anchor needs, so reusing it adds a guarantee without adding an operator. RECORDED ALTERNATIVE: an RFC 3161 timestamp authority, which a §5.2 issuer-registry deployment needs instead, since such a deployment may run no log at all. Stapled at signing time, so dispute-time verification never depends on a service endpoint still being reachable years later.

log_id.description: Identifier of the §5.2 transparency log this signature is anchored in.

epoch.description: Log epoch whose cosigned head covers this entry — the same epoch space a supersession record advances (§5.2, §7).

inclusion_proof.description: Merkle audit path from this signature's leaf to the epoch head, ordered leaf-ward to root-ward, each sibling hash base64url unpadded. PROFILE-DEFINED: leaf encoding and the log's hash function.

hash.description: PROFILE-DEFINED hash encoding. Profile v1: SHA-256 over the JCS (RFC 8785) serialization, base64url without padding, prefixed with the algorithm name.

kid.description: Key identifier of the signing key. PROFILE-DEFINED: the derivation. Profile v1 uses `base64url(SHA-256(SPKI DER))` without padding \u2014 the unpadded base64url encoding of the SHA-256 digest of the DER-encoded SubjectPublicKeyInfo of the signing public key. The identifier is therefore CONTENT-DERIVED and unambiguous without consulting any directory; a key directory only RESOLVES a `kid` to its material and validity interval, it never defines it. REQUIRED, and deliberately not optional: evidence signed without a key identifier is verifiable only by trial-verification against every historical key, which goes ambiguous the instant two keys coexist. This field is NOT retrofittable \u2014 artifacts already signed without it can never be cleanly verified after a rotation, which is why it is present from the first commit. RECORDED ALTERNATIVE: an RFC 7638 JWK thumbprint, which is equally content-derived but fixes the key representation to JWK rather than SPKI.

alg.description: Signature algorithm identifier, JOSE/COSE name. PROFILE-DEFINED: the disclosure constrains no algorithm suite. Profile v1 admits exactly this set \u2014 ES256/ES384/ES512, the ECDSA suite AP2 v0.2 requires of its bindings; EdDSA (Ed25519); and RS256/PS256, which appear on deployed WebAuthn authenticators. A binding profile MAY narrow this enum but MUST NOT widen it without taking a new profile identifier. This member REPLACES the former free-string `algorithm`: a free string and a constrained identifier naming the same fact can disagree, and disagreement about the algorithm is disagreement about what the signature covers.

signed_at.description: The signing instant, RFC 3339 with 'Z' and second precision \u2014 the same timestamp form every other timestamp in this repository uses (PROFILE-DEFINED, decided; profile v1 takes no epoch-integer form, so that a validity interval and an artifact's `issued_at`/`expiry` are always directly comparable). This is the instant that key-validity intervals are evaluated AGAINST: a signature verifies iff `signed_at` falls inside the [not_before, not_after] interval recorded for `kid`, and a verifier MUST verify against THE KEY CURRENT AT SIGNING TIME, NEVER THE KEY CURRENT NOW. Rejecting evidence because its signing key was rotated afterwards is a bug, not a security property \u2014 planned retirement is prospective only, and evidence anchored before it stays valid permanently. A self-asserted `signed_at` is adequate for routine verification and NOT adequate for dispute-grade evidence; see `anchor`.

ds_tag.description: \u00a76.2 domain-separation tag: the digest of the domain separator this signature is bound to, base64url unpadded. DISPOSITION (PROFILE-DEFINED, DECIDED \u2014 this is the choice the schema makes rather than leaves implicit): profile v1 carries `ds_tag` HERE, in the JSON body, beside the `domain_separation` components it is derived from, AND requires it to byte-equal the domain separator bound into the carrier's signed input \u2014 the WebAuthn `clientDataJSON.challenge`, or the KB-JWT `aud`/`nonce` under an SD-JWT binding. A verifier MUST recompute the tag from `domain_separation` and MUST compare it against the value bound in the carrier; a body `ds_tag` not reproduced in the carrier is NOT covered by the signature and MUST be rejected. The body copy exists so that evidence can be checked offline without a carrier parser; the carrier copy is what makes the separator signature-covered. Leaving this disposition implicit is exactly what \u00a76.2's transplant attack needs in order to succeed, because two verifiers would otherwise disagree about whether the separator is signature-covered at all. RECORDED ALTERNATIVE: carry the tag ENTIRELY in the WebAuthn/KB-JWT layer and leave only the components in the body \u2014 rejected for v1 because it makes offline evidence verification depend on a carrier parser, and because body components carrying no tag invite a verifier to treat them as authoritative when nothing signs them. PROFILE-DEFINED derivation, profile v1: SHA-256 over the ASCII prefix 'MandateLifecycle/v1/transcript' followed by LP(purpose), LP(audience), LP(relying_party), LP(mandate_family_id), LP(decimal encoding of mandate_version), LP(rail), LP(binding_profile), where LP(x) is the uint16 big-endian byte length of the UTF-8 encoding of x followed by those bytes \u2014 length-prefixed with NO delimiters, because `relying_party` and `mandate_family_id` are attacker-influenced. The prefix MUST differ from the \u00a77 nullifier prefix ('MandateLifecycle/v1/nullifier') so that a transcript tag and a nullifier tag can never collide.

anchor.description: OPTIONAL but RECOMMENDED \u2014 see the `$defs/anchor` description. Omit it and `signed_at` is self-asserted, which does not carry dispute-grade weight, because the signer is precisely the party with an incentive to misstate the signing time.
